arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 27: he stayed away from Cafe Nahat, but Dana phoned at 12:19 and set Sat 13:00 at Nahat to tell him about Haifa herself; he said yes, warmly. Sat Nov 28: she tells him all of it (a cafe by the port, January, answer by Mon Dec 7) and asks what he wants. He says 'I want you to be happy'. She: 'I have until the seventh. So do you.' Next: he goes quiet again; Sun Dec 6 he says it plainly.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26: the run 'went out', his batch is Monday; Monday before ten in writing. Fri Nov 27 16:09 Gadi phoned on Shabbat eve 'just to wish a peaceful Shabbat', said 'Sunday payment run', then 'Monday before ten, written in stone'. Next: Mon Nov 30 the money doesn't come; week 3 Gadi asks for January and Ishai gets angry for the first time.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 27: the challah, 'apologising by disappearing'; Ishai: 'tomorrow I ask the questions'. Tomer that night: 'she sounds wrecked'. Sat Nov 28 (reveal) after havdalah: dinner just them; he overhears her call with Shir (the lamp, three years) and she tells him: Shir moved out in October, there were no plumbers. For once he takes care of her: she stays the night on his armchair. Next: week 4, not fine yet but not alone; Tomer keeps showing up.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi and Eli
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 27: he wrote to Eli (two grey ticks); Shabbat soup with Mrs. Levi ('busy is what I say about Eli'); his phone buzzed face down. Sat Nov 28 after havdalah: it was Eli: landing Monday, 'don't tell her, I want to see her face'. Ishai and Moti plan to keep her home Monday. Next: Eli lands Mon Nov 30.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 27: Avi took his keys back (cousin Shimon 'knows nothing, free advice'), kept the flyer 'just in case', told Ishai Dana asked if he was sick; at 18:15 he climbed the stairs with leftover pitas. Next: week 4 a sufganiyot queue round the block; open.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Thu Nov 26, lesson 4, the last Noa paid for: in a scene with a barista who is leaving he says 'I want you to stay' and 'I'll learn the timetable'. He signs up for the next course (from Dec 10) at full price, himself. Yael: 'now the real one'.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Wed Nov 25: Lior let Haifa slip, 'chapter fifteen is ruined'. Sat Nov 28: typing in the corner at Nahat while Dana and Ishai talk, very fast. Moshe: fewer aphids. Next: Sun Nov 29 Ishai reads chapter one for the cover and recognises himself.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 27 21:05: let himself in with the old spare key, ate cold pasta, 'Noa sounds wrecked', 'you check on her'. Sat Nov 28: PixelPlex with Ishai (A Midsummer Night's Dream, engine); Ishai tells him Noa needed a couch, and Tomer texts her three times during the film. Next: he keeps showing up for her.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: First night Mon Nov 23: 91 up. Tue Nov 24 Ishai lent Yossi 200, 'don't tell Boaz'. Next: second night Mon Dec 7, Yossi pays back in coins.

beats.goal: Shabbat morning, still a little foggy. Ishai walks Falafel in the park (the dog on his leash). Mr. Zelig is on his bench counting pigeons. Ishai tells him he is meeting the barista at one and she will tell him about Haifa herself. Zelig: when someone tells you their news, they are really asking you something; listen for the question, and answer that one. Ishai says he'll try. Gentle, odd, warm.
beats.teaser: Shabbat morning in the park. Mr. Zelig has advice about listening.
beats.forceText: On his Shabbat walk with Falafel, Mr. Zelig tells Ishai to listen for the question inside the barista's news.

forceLines.say: When someone tells you news, they are asking you something. Listen for the question.

forceCommentary.say: Life advice from a man who talks to pigeons. Take it, babe.
He counted the pigeons twice. Same number. Suspicious.

moments.text: Fog lifting off the pond. Ishai walks Falafel along the path; Mr. Zelig sits on his bench in a Shabbat jacket, a paper bag of crumbs on his knee.

lines.say: Forty-one. No. Forty. One is a crow pretending.
Shabbat shalom, Mr. Zelig.
Shabbat shalom. Your dog walks you very well.
He's had practice. I'm slow on Saturdays.
Everybody is slow on Saturdays. Except pigeons.
Don't they rest?
They rest standing up. Like you.
I'm not resting. I'm... waiting for one o'clock.
The barista.
How do you always know?
You have a one o'clock face.
She's going to tell me about Haifa. Herself, this time.
Good. The wrong mouth is done.
And I'll say something smart. Hopefully.
Don't say smart. Say true.
Those are different?
Very. Smart is for exams.

commentary.say: A one o'clock face. I have a two-hour-reality-show face.
Forty pigeons and a crow in disguise. Finally, reliable data.

then.text: Mr. Zelig scatters a handful of crumbs; Falafel strains at the leash and Ishai holds him back while the pigeons settle.

moments.text: Ishai sits on the end of the bench. Falafel lies down under it, eyes on the pigeons. Mr. Zelig folds the empty crumb bag very neatly.

lines.say: When someone tells you their news, they are asking you something.
Asking what?
Every time it's different. Listen for the question.
And if I don't hear one?
Then you weren't listening. You were rehearsing.
I do rehearse. In the shower. Badly.
The pigeons rehearse also. Then a bus comes.
What do I do if I hear it?
You answer that one. Not the easy one next to it.
There's always an easy one next to it.
Always. It's very comfortable. Like this bench.
Okay. Listen for the question.
And don't bring the dog. Dogs make people say nice things.
Nice things are bad?
Today, nice is the easy one.

commentary.say: 'Nice is the easy one.' Moshe has been saying that for weeks. Silently.
One o'clock, Cafe Nahat. Listen for the question, Ishai. I'm begging you.

update.memory: Told Ishai on Shabbat: when someone tells you news, they ask you something; listen for the question, answer that one, not the easy nice one.

beats.goal: Dana set this herself on Friday: one o'clock at Cafe Nahat, so she can tell him about Haifa in person. A slow Saturday shift; Lior types in the corner. She sits with him and tells him all of it: a new cafe by the port in Haifa, she would run it, from January, and she must answer by Monday December 7. Then she asks what he thinks, and then what he WANTS. He hears the question and still takes the easy one: 'I want you to be happy.' She is not angry, just tired: 'I have until the seventh. So do you.' She goes back behind the counter. A real setback; no kiss, no fight.
beats.teaser: One o'clock at Cafe Nahat. Dana tells him herself.
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat Dana tells Ishai about Haifa herself and asks what he wants. He says he wants her to be happy.

forceLines.say: I didn't ask what's good for me. I asked what you want.
I want you to be happy.

forceCommentary.say: He heard the question. He answered the one next to it. Babe.
'I want you to be happy.' The receipt of feelings.

moments.text: Cafe Nahat on a slow Saturday. Dana brings two cups to the corner table and sits down across from Ishai; Lior types in the far corner and doesn't look up.

lines.say: You came.
You said one. It's one.
Twelve fifty-eight. Showing off.
I didn't wear the grey shirt.
Noa?
Noa. Twice. By phone.
Good. Drink. I made it, so it's drinkable.
No leaf today?
I didn't know what to draw.
That's... fair.
Three days, Ishai. Avi thought you were sick.
I wasn't sick. I was—
Busy. Friday. I read it.
It was a bad text.
It was a terrible text. Tomer agrees, apparently.
Tomer agrees with everyone. Loudly.

commentary.say: No leaf on the cup. Nobody panic. I'm panicking.
Lior's typing speed just doubled. Literature is happening at table six.

then.text: They both drink at the same time and put the cups down at the same time; Dana almost laughs and doesn't.

moments.text: Dana turns her cup round and round on the saucer. Ishai sits very straight. Across the room Lior's keyboard has gone quiet.

lines.say: Okay. Properly. From me, not from Lior.
Okay.
A new cafe in Haifa. By the port. Big windows.
Sounds beautiful.
They want me to run it. All of it. From January.
Run it. Wow. That's—
I have to answer by the seventh. December.
The seventh. Monday week.
So. What do you think?
I think it's a big chance.
It is.
And you'd be great. You'd be so good at it.
I know I'd be good at it.
Then... it's a good offer.
Ishai. I didn't ask what's good for me.
No?
I asked what you think. Now I'm asking what you want.

commentary.say: There it is. The question. Mr. Zelig is somewhere nodding at a pigeon.
Listen for the question, babe. It's right there on the saucer.

moments.text: A long pause. Ishai looks at his cup, at the window, at the cup again. Dana waits; then she stands and picks up her tray.

lines.say: What I want.
What you want. It's a short question.
I want... I want you to be happy.
Hm.
That's true. I do.
I know. That's what people say at airports.
Dana—
It's okay. Really. It's nice.
Nice is the easy one. Someone told me that today.
Someone was right.
Can I... think?
I have until the seventh, Ishai. So do you.
Okay. The seventh.
Finish the coffee. It's drinkable, I promised.
Thank you. For telling me yourself.
I wanted it from me. The rest I wanted from you.

commentary.say: He knew it was the easy one. He SAID it was the easy one. And took it.
Two deadlines, one date. Moshe would have said 'stay'. Moshe is a plant.

update.memory: Told Ishai about Haifa myself: the port cafe, January, answer by Dec 7. Asked what he wants. He said 'I want you to be happy'. I said: until the seventh, you too.

beats.goal: Shabbat ends at 17:16. Alone at home Ishai makes havdalah, then finally turns over the phone that buzzed during Friday's dinner. It was Eli in Toronto, answering his text: he lands Monday at two in the afternoon; 'don't tell her, I want to see her face'. Ishai phones Moti (the only other one who knows how long it has been) and they plan to keep Mrs. Levi at home on Monday afternoon without her guessing. Moti is gruff and moved. No one tells Mrs. Levi.
beats.teaser: Shabbat ends. The phone that buzzed at dinner finally gets turned over.
beats.forceText: After havdalah Ishai reads the text from Friday: Eli lands Monday and wants to surprise his mother. Ishai phones Moti to plan it.

forceLines.say: Moti, it's Ishai. Eli lands Monday. Two o'clock. She can't know.
Four years. And he lands on a Monday. Fine. Monday.

forceCommentary.say: Toronto answered! I'm not crying, the havdalah candle is smoky.
Moti, keeper of stair lights and secrets. Strong week for Moti.

moments.text: Three stars over Herzl Street. Ishai says havdalah at the window by Moshe, puts the candle out in the wine, then turns his phone over. A Toronto number, from Friday night.

lines.say: Eli. 'Landing Monday, two in the afternoon. Don't tell her. I want to see her face.'
Falafel. He's coming. He's actually coming.

commentary.say: The buzz at dinner was TORONTO. Not the barista. Toronto!
Shavua tov. The week starts with a plot twist and a damp wick.

moments.text: Ishai paces between the desk and the window with the phone at his ear, Falafel's head turning after him each time.

lines.say: Moti, shavua tov. It's Ishai, from four.
I know who it is. You're the quiet one. What happened?
Eli answered. He lands Monday. Two o'clock.
Eli. Her Eli?
Her Eli. And he says don't tell her.
Four years, and he comes like a thief. Typical.
He wants to see her face.
So do I. I've wanted to for four years.
Monday afternoon she has to be home. Not at the clinic, not the market.
Leave it to me. I'll bring my blood pressure machine.
Your blood pressure?
She loves to tell me it's high. Two hours, minimum.
That's perfect. Moti, that's brilliant.
I'm the committee. Logistics is what I do.
And the stair light?
Paid in full. He'll see her face in good light.
Don't tell anyone. Not even Boaz.
Especially not Boaz. He tells his whole bus.

commentary.say: A surprise run by the building committee. Minutes will be taken.
Moti's blood pressure, weaponised for love. I adore this building.

update.memory: Ishai told me Eli lands Monday at two and wants to surprise her. I'll keep her home with my blood pressure machine. Not a word to Boaz.

beats.goal: The dinner Noa set on Friday, just the two of them, 'about you'. Ishai makes shakshuka. She comes too bright and wants the Dana report; he gives it, then holds her to 'tonight I ask the questions'. Her phone buzzes again ('nobody'); he tells her to answer. She takes it at the window, back turned, low voice, and he hears enough: Shir, three years, splitting a lamp, a box to leave with Shir's sister. She hangs up and sees his face. She breaks: Shir moved out in October, she told nobody, there were never any plumbers, saying it makes it true, and she pushed his love life because hers ended. For once he takes care of her: no sorry, he says what he wants, she stays tonight. She makes him go to the film with Tomer anyway and stays on his armchair under the good blanket with Falafel.
beats.teaser: Dinner, just the two of them. Tonight Ishai asks the questions.
beats.forceText: Over dinner Ishai overhears Noa on the phone with Shir. She tells him: Shir moved out in October. He makes her stay the night.

forceLines.say: She moved out in October. There were never any plumbers.
You're staying here tonight. That's not a question.

forceCommentary.say: Three years. A lamp. And she carried it alone since October. Oh, Noa.
No plumbers. Ever. The kitchen floor was never a lake.

moments.text: Ishai cracks eggs into a pan of tomatoes and peppers on the hob. Noa sits at the island in her big coat, too cheerful, tearing the last of yesterday's challah.

lines.say: Shavua tov. So. One o'clock. Report.
Shavua tov. Blue shirt, as ordered.
I saw. Good boy. And?
She told me everything. Haifa. January. The seventh.
And you said?
'I want you to be happy.'
No.
Yes.
Ishai. That's what people say at airports.
That's exactly what she said.
Smart woman. Wasted on you. For now.
Okay. Report over.
It's not over, we haven't fixed it—
Noa. Tonight I ask the questions. You promised.
I said maybe.
You said 'tomorrow'. It's tomorrow.
Your eggs are burning.
They're not. Nice try.

commentary.say: 'Your eggs are burning.' The oldest exit in the book. The eggs are fine.
He's holding the line! On a shakshuka! Growth!

then.text: Ishai sets the pan on a board between them and hands her a spoon; they eat straight from the pan, the challah going in turn.

moments.text: They eat from the pan. Noa's phone buzzes in her coat, stops, buzzes again. Ishai just looks at the pocket. She takes it to the window and turns her back.

lines.say: Answer it. Nobody has called six times.
Fine. One minute. Eat.
Hi. ...No, I'm at Ishai's.
I said keep the lamp. You bought the lamp.
Three years, Shir. And we're dividing a lamp.
No. Don't come for the box. I'll leave it with your sister.
Noa?
I have to go. Bye. ...Bye.
Noa.
How much did you hear?
Shir. Three years. A lamp.
The lamp is a long story.
I have time. I have a whole pan.
Don't be nice. If you're nice I'll cry.
Then I'll be a little nice.
Ishai...

commentary.say: 'Three years, Shir.' And there it is. The name on the phone, finally out loud.
A box for the sister. A lamp for Shir. Breakups are mostly furniture.

moments.text: Noa sits back down at the island and puts her face in her hands. Ishai comes round, sits on the stool next to her and doesn't say anything yet.

lines.say: She moved out. October. The second week.
October. That's... seven weeks.
Seven weeks and two days. I'm counting too.
The plumbers?
There were never any plumbers. The floor was dry.
Noa...
My flat echoes. That's why your couch. Your armchair.
Why didn't you tell me?
Because saying it makes it true.
It was true anyway.
And you were finally happy. Dana, the basil, the class.
So you pushed me.
Somebody should get the happy part.
You don't get to take care of me and hide this.
I know.
I want you to stay here tonight. That's not a question.
Look at you. Saying what you want.

commentary.say: 'Somebody should get the happy part.' I need a minute. Oren, hold my mic.
He said what he wants. To the wrong woman, for the right reason. It counts.

then.text: Ishai fetches the good blanket from the closet and wraps it round her shoulders; Falafel puts his chin on her knee and leaves it there.

moments.text: Noa in the armchair under the good blanket, a mug of tea in both hands, Falafel's head on her knee. Ishai looks at the clock: the film is at nine.

lines.say: I'll text Tomer. I'm not going.
You're going.
Noa, I'm not leaving you here alone.
I'm not alone. I have a dog.
Falafel doesn't count.
Falafel counts double. Look at him.
What do I tell Tomer?
Tell him... I'm okay. Not fine. Okay.
Okay is good.
Okay is a start. Go see the fairies.
Donkey head. Four lovers. Shakespeare.
Tell me if anyone ends up with the right person.
I'll take notes.
Leave the hall light on when you go.
I'll leave all of them on.
Ishush. Thank you. Don't say sorry.
I wasn't going to.

commentary.say: Falafel counts double. Finally someone said it on air.
'Okay, not fine.' The most honest word on this show all season.

update.memory: Told Ishai about Shir at last: she moved out in October, no plumbers. He made me stay the night and go easy on myself. He sent me 'okay' to tell Tomer.

beats.goal: Home from the PixelPlex. Noa is still awake in his armchair under the good blanket, Falafel at her feet, every light on as he promised. She asks whether anyone ended up with the right person. She mentions Tomer texted her three times during the film and asks whether Ishai told him; Ishai only told him she needed a couch. She switches her phone off for the first time in weeks. Quiet, kind, short; then lights out, Noa in the armchair, Ishai in bed.
beats.teaser: After the film, someone is still awake in his armchair.
beats.forceText: Back from the film, Ishai finds Noa awake in the armchair. Tomer texted her three times. She switches her phone off.

forceLines.say: Tomer texted me three times. During Shakespeare. Did you tell him?
Only that you needed a couch. That's all.

forceCommentary.say: Three texts in one film. Tomer, sweetie, we see you.
She switched the phone off. Shir gets a lamp. Noa gets a night's sleep.

moments.text: Ishai lets himself in. Every light is on. Noa sits up in the armchair under the good blanket; Falafel thumps his tail on the floor and doesn't get up.

lines.say: Well? Did anyone end up with the right person?
Eventually. After a potion. And a donkey head.
So it takes magic.
It takes a very confused forest.
Was Tomer good?
Tomer laughed at the donkey for ten minutes.
He texted me. Three times. During Shakespeare.
Three? He told me his phone was off.
Did you tell him?
Only that you needed a couch. Nothing else.
He asked if I'd eaten. And if I want burekas tomorrow.
That's Tomer.
Hm. That's Tomer.
What did you answer?
'Okay.' He'll understand 'okay'.
He understands everything. Eventually. Like the forest.

commentary.say: Three texts during a play he paid to see. That's not a friend checking in, Oren.
Burekas as a love language. Tomer is fluent.

then.text: Ishai switches off the lights one by one, leaving the small one by the window on; Noa watches him, then holds up her phone.

moments.text: In the light of the small lamp by Moshe, Noa holds her phone up so he can see her switch it off. She pulls the blanket up. Ishai sits on the edge of his bed.

lines.say: Look. Off. First time since October.
How does it feel?
Quiet. Your fridge is very loud.
It's an old fridge. It has a lot to say.
Goodnight, Ishush.
Goodnight. Wake me if the flat echoes.
Your flat doesn't echo. That's the whole point.
Then sleep.

commentary.say: Lights out. Moshe, Falafel and two tired humans. Full house.
Phone off for Noa. And Dana's question still on for him. Until the seventh.

update.memory: Slept on Ishai's armchair after telling him about Shir. Switched my phone off for the first time since October. Tomer texted three times; I said okay.

hook.text: Noa is asleep in his armchair, phone off. Tomer texted her three times during the film. And Dana's question waits until the seventh.

previously.text: He kept Shabbat and never turned the phone over. Dana's coffee at one stands. Tomer let himself in at nine: Noa 'sounds wrecked'. 'I'll check on her tomorrow.'

hosts: Saturday. Shabbat until 17:16. The flat is quiet and the phone is still face down.
Somewhere under that phone is a buzz from Friday dinner. He hasn't looked. Strong man.
One o'clock at Cafe Nahat. Dana set it herself. Clocks are being watched.
Noa said tonight is 'about him'. Ishai said tonight he asks the questions. One of them is wrong.
Fog over Herzl Street this morning. Very moody. Very fitting.
Moshe has fewer aphids this week. Oren has been unbearable about it.
Fewer aphids. I'm just saying it again because it's good news and we need some.
Falafel slept fourteen hours. Professional. A Siberian Hascii knows how to do a Saturday.
Saturday nap at two. The most reliable appointment in his diary.
Tonight at the PixelPlex: A Midsummer Night's Dream. Tomer is paying for popcorn. Allegedly.
Tomer raided the fridge last night and promised large popcorn. We'll be checking receipts.
Shakespeare, lovers in a forest, a potion. No parallels to this show whatsoever.
Tomer let himself in with a three-year-old spare key. Every building needs one Tomer.
Avi climbed four flights with pitas last night. Avi doesn't climb stairs for nothing.
Mrs. Levi said 'busy' is her word for Eli. Ishai went very quiet after that.
Noa called twice about the grey shirt with the ink stain. The shirt is a character now.
Blue shirt today. If he wears the grey one, Noa will feel it from across town.
Lior has written fourteen chapters. Nobody has read one. That will change.
Gadi phoned on Shabbat eve 'just to wish a peaceful Shabbat'. Nobody calls just to wish.
Monday before ten. In writing. Written in stone, Gadi says. Stone is famously flexible.
Noa's 'nobody' called again yesterday. Nobody is very persistent, Oren.
Tonight Noa and Ishai, just them. Viewers know what he doesn't. Be gentle with her.
Seven weeks of plumbers. No plumber in Tel Aviv works that slowly.
After havdalah buses come back. Before it, Herzl Street belongs to cats and joggers.
Next Saturday's film is A Christmas Carol. Three ghosts. Ishai can relate.
A weekend of deadlines: Dana's is the seventh. Gadi's is Monday. Moshe's is never.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Saturday edition. Slow songs for slow people.
Fog this morning, partly cloudy later. Fifteen degrees. Wear the jacket your mother bought.
No traffic report today. There is no traffic. There are three cats on Allenby.
This one goes out to everyone waiting for a reply. Two grey ticks, we feel you.
A listener asks if it's rude to answer a call during dinner. Depends on the dinner.
Saturday cooking tip: shakshuka forgives everything except too much cumin.
Coming up: forty minutes without talking. Mostly because I'm eating.
A song for people who say 'I'm fine'. You know who you are.
Shavua tov from Radio Herzl. Buses are back, the kiosk queue is forming.
Tonight, a quiz: what's the most common lie in Tel Aviv? Answer: 'I'm on my way.'
If your phone's been off all Shabbat, sorry. It's been a busy day for your group chats.
Weather for tonight: dry, cool, a little moon. Good for walking home from somewhere.

zelig: Forty pigeons. Forty-one if the crow is honest.
On Shabbat even the ducks walk slower.
A question is a door. People keep painting the frame.
My wife answered questions very quickly. I'm still answering hers.
michal: Saturday morning, only the serious ones.
Nobody comes to run club on Fridays. Including me.
sivan: The quiet guy with the dog skipped this week. Weak.
lior: Chapter one. The man and his coffee. Too obvious? No. Keep it.
He came back. Good. Chapter sixteen can start.
Don't look up. Writers don't look up.
She asked what he wants. Write that down. Exactly that.
kobi: Saturday night system: odd numbers only.
After nine, everything is a good idea.
Shakespeare? In my day we had Saturday football.
Another round. The system says so.

street: ...the kiosk opens after havdalah, he said, not a minute before...
...my grandmother still won't use the lift on Shabbat...
...no, the fog was worse in Jaffa...
...he says he's coming, he's been saying that since summer...
market: ...closed till Sunday, come back tomorrow for the dates...
...the spice man says the cumin is from his cousin...
park: ...she wants to bring the stroller and the dog, both...
...that old man counts pigeons every day, I swear...
...shabbat shalom, is it gone noon already?...
...the duck has a name, my son decided, it's Gideon...
cafe: ...a cafe in Haifa? who leaves Tel Aviv for Haifa?...
...two flat whites and whatever the quiet guy has...
...the writer in the corner never orders a second cup...
...she didn't draw anything on it today, did you notice?...

chat.say: Shavua tov all. The stair light worked all Shabbat. Moti thanks everyone. No more coins.
Shavua tov. Who is frying onions? It smells very good. Just asking.
Anyone have a spare light bulb, the small kind? Will return a big one.
Reminder: blue bins Sunday morning. The truck comes at seven, he does not wait.
My game show was a rerun. I knew every answer. Again.
Monday afternoon Moti will be busy with committee business. Please don't knock at Apt 1.
